Translation of the passage:

[La] is an extra particle (zā'ida) ﴿I swear by this city﴾ (Makkah)

﴿And you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿are lawful (حِلّ) [i.e., permitted, حَلال]﴾ ﴿in this city﴾, meaning that it is lawful for you to fight in it. God fulfilled this promise to him on the Day of the Conquest. Thus the sentence is a parenthetical insertion (i'tirāḍ) between the thing sworn by (al-muqsam bihi) and what is conjoined to it.
﴿And by the begetter and what he begot﴾, that is, Adam, ﴿and what he begot﴾, that is, his offspring. Here "mā" (what) means "man" (who).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 90, verse 4:

﴿Indeed, We created man﴾ i.e., mankind (al-jins) ﴿in toil﴾ (kabad), meaning fatigue and hardship; he endures the calamities of this world and the severities of the Hereafter.

﴿Does he think﴾ means: does the human (al-insan), meaning the strong man of Quraysh, who is Abu al-Ashudd ibn Kaladah, suppose, because of his strength, ﴿that no one will have power over him﴾? Here "anna" is the lightened form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy form (thaqilah), and its noun is omitted, meaning that he ﴿will never have power over him, anyone﴾, while Allah is capable of him.
﴿He says, "I have squandered"﴾ in hostility toward Muhammad ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, much of it piled one upon another.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 90, verse 7:

﴿Does he think that﴾ meaning, that ﴿no one has seen him﴾ in what he spent, so that he would know its amount. But Allah knows its amount, and that it is not of what one boasts about; and He will recompense him for his wicked deed.
﴿Did We not make﴾ is an interrogative of affirmation (*istifham taqrir*, a question that asks the listener to confirm a known fact), meaning: We did make "for him two eyes."

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 90, verse 10:**

﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾: We made clear to him the path of good and the path of evil.

﴿فَلا﴾ meaning فَهَلّا (fahalla), "why did he not"
﴿اِقْتَحَمَ العَقَبَة﴾ meaning جاوَزَها (jawazaha), "cross it" / "pass over it"

﴿Wa ma adraka﴾ "And what made you know" (meaning: made you know) ﴿ma al-'aqaba﴾ "what the steep path is," ﴿allati yaqtahimuha﴾ "which he attempts," glorifying its status. The sentence is an *i'tiraD* (parenthetical interjection), and it explains the reason for its permissibility.
﴿Freeing a neck﴾ from slavery, by manumitting it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 90, verse 14:

﴿Or feeding on a day of severe hunger﴾ (maj'ah), a time of famine

Verse 15: ﴿An orphan with near kinship﴾ — "qarabah" (kinship).

Note: The Arabic gloss in the source is "قَرابَة" (qarabah), meaning "kinship." The verse itself, ﴿يَتِيمًا ذا مَقْرَبَة﴾, is translated above as "An orphan with near kinship."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 90, verse 16:

﴿Or a needy person covered in dust﴾ (lit. "lying in the dust"), clinging to the earth because of his poverty. In another reading, the two verbs are replaced by two nouns in the nominative: the first is made genitive by addition to "riqabah" (raqabah, "a neck"), and the second is given tanwin (nunation), so that "iqtiham" (iqtiḥām, "forcing one's way through") is understood to precede "al-'aqabah" (al-'aqabah, "the steep path"). The aforementioned reading explains it.

Then he was among those who believed and enjoined one another to patience (تَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْر), and enjoined one another to compassion.

Note on the Arabic: the verb "ثُمَّ كانَ" is connected (ʿaṭf) to "اِقْتَحَمَ" (iqtaḥama, "he broke through/undertook the steep ascent"), and "ثُمَّ" (thumma, "then") here indicates sequence in mention (lil-tartīb al-dhikrī), not necessarily sequence in time. The meaning is: "and it was at the time of the ascent [that he was] among those who believed and enjoined one another..."

Translation of the commentary:

"Then he was" is joined (ʿaṭf) to "he broke through" (iqtaḥama), and "then" (thumma) denotes sequence of mention (al-tartīb al-dhikrī), and the meaning is: he was at the time of the breaking-through "among those who believed and enjoined one another" — they advised one another (awṣā baʿḍuhum baʿḍan) "to patience" (bi-al-ṣabr) in obedience to God and abstaining from disobedience, and "they enjoined one another to compassion" (wa-tawāṣaw bi-al-marḥama), that is, mercy toward creation.
Those (﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾) who are described by these attributes are ﴿the companions of the right hand﴾ (أصْحاب المَيْمَنَة), meaning the people of the right (اليَمِين).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 90, verse 19:

﴿And those who disbelieved in Our signs, they are the companions of the left hand﴾ (al-Shimal), i.e., the left side.
﴿Upon them is a Fire closed in.﴾ With the hamza, and the waw is its substitute (in the reading mawsadah). Mutbaqah (sealed over).
